title: Festivals and everyday culture
job: Talk about what is happening around you
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: qui IS THE SUBJECT OF ITS CLAUSE AND que IS THE OBJECT — WHATEVER THEY POINT AT. une fête QUI dure cinq jours (the fête does the lasting), les gens QUE j'aime (I do the loving, the gens are done to). English chooses between who and which by whether the thing is a person, which is no help at all here: French never asks that question. Look at the verb behind the word instead — if a subject is missing, it is qui.

que ELIDES BEFORE A VOWEL AND qui NEVER DOES. les gâteaux QU'ON fait, but les gens QUI ont un cadeau — qui keeps all three letters however the next word starts. A learner who has learnt one elision rule applies it to both and writes qu'i, which is not a word. This is the half of the pair that costs marks.

THE ARTICLE IS THE TENSE ON A DAY OF THE WEEK. dimanche is THIS Sunday, once; LE dimanche is every Sunday, as a habit. Je pars dimanche against Le dimanche je ne travaille pas. Spanish and Italian split the same way, and English needs on Sunday against on Sundays to do it.
AND A BARE DAY TAKES NO PREPOSITION AT ALL. Je pars dimanche, not *je pars sur dimanche or *à dimanche. English's on has nothing to translate to, which is exactly why a learner reaches for one.

A DATE IS le + THE PLAIN NUMBER + THE MONTH, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS AN ORDINAL. le quatorze juillet, le vingt-cinq décembre — but le premier mai, with L2-M4's premier. English needs the fourteenth of July and French needs the fourteen July; the of is not there either.

MONTHS AND DAYS ARE LOWERCASE IN FRENCH: janvier, mai, juillet, août, décembre, dimanche. Only the festivals are capitalised — Noël, Pâques, le Nouvel An. English capitalises all of them, so this is a habit to unlearn rather than a rule to learn.

A CUSTOM IS DESCRIBED WITH L3-M8's IMPERSONAL on: à Noël on mange en famille, à Pâques on offre des cadeaux. It is what everybody does, with nobody named — and it is the natural voice for explaining your own culture to somebody who has never seen it. dont, the relative for de, is real and is L4's.

sentences.display: C'est une fête qui dure cinq jours
sentences.cue: It's a festival that lasts five days
sentences.literal: It-is a festival which lasts five days

words.note: Feminine. It covers a public holiday and a Saturday night alike; faire la fête is to party, and la fête nationale is in S06.
The SUBJECT of the clause behind it, person or thing alike. It never elides: qui a, qui est, qui on — always four letters and never qu'.
Regular -er: une fête qui dure, deux fêtes qui durent. Not to be confused with dur, hard.

sentences.trap: English picks who for people and which for things. French picks qui when the word is the subject of what follows, and that is a different question with a different answer.
sentences.sound: seh oon FET kee dewr sank ZHOOR.

variations.display: C'est une fête qui dure deux jours
variations.cue: It's a festival that lasts two days
variations.changed: the number moves; the relative does not

variations.display: C'est une fête qui est pour les enfants
variations.cue: It's a festival that's for children
variations.changed: qui in front of est, still the subject

mistake.display: C'est une fête que dure cinq jours
mistake.why: dure has no subject without it, so the word is qui. C'est une fête qui dure cinq jours.

sentences.usage: Explaining a festival of your own to someone who has never heard of it.
sentences.mnemonic: If the verb behind it has lost its subject, the word is qui.

sentences.display: Les gens que j'aime sont ici
sentences.cue: The people I love are here
sentences.literal: The people whom I love are here

words.note: Always plural, and it takes no singular — one person is une personne. les gens sont, never les gens est.

sentences.trap: English drops the relative altogether — the people I love. French cannot: que has to be written, even when nothing in English marks it.
sentences.sound: lay zhahn kuh zhem son tee-SEE.

variations.display: Les gens qui sont ici sont mes amis
variations.cue: The people who are here are my friends
variations.changed: qui now, because sont has no other subject

variations.display: Les gens que j'aime sont à la fête
variations.cue: The people I love are at the festival
variations.changed: the same que, a different place

mistake.why: The relative is never dropped in French. Les gens que j'aime sont ici.

sentences.usage: Saying who matters to you, in a sentence English would leave half-built.
sentences.mnemonic: English can leave it out; French never can.

sentences.display: Les gâteaux qu'on fait sont pour Noël
sentences.cue: The cakes we make are for Christmas
sentences.literal: The cakes that-one makes are for Christmas

words.note: que elided onto on, written as one word. que on is never written — the e goes, exactly as it did in L3-M5's qu'il and qu'elle.
The plural of le gâteau, with the -x that -eau nouns take instead of an -s. Nothing is heard: gâteau and gâteaux sound the same.
Masculine and capitalised, and it takes à for the occasion: à Noël on mange en famille. The tree is le sapin de Noël.

sentences.trap: qu'on is one written word and two spoken ones. Writing que on marks a learner instantly, and hearing it is no help at all — the elision is silent.
sentences.sound: lay ga-TOH kon feh son poor no-EL.

variations.display: Les gâteaux qu'on fait sont pour la fête
variations.cue: The cakes we make are for the party
variations.changed: the same relative, a different occasion

variations.display: Les gâteaux que j'aime sont ici
variations.cue: The cakes I like are here
variations.changed: que unelided, because j' is not on

mistake.display: Les gâteaux que on fait sont pour Noël
mistake.why: que loses its e in front of a vowel. Les gâteaux qu'on fait.

sentences.usage: Describing what a household actually does at a festival, rather than what a book says.
sentences.mnemonic: que meets a vowel and loses its e; qui never does.

sentences.display: À Noël on mange en famille
sentences.cue: At Christmas we eat with family
sentences.literal: At Christmas one eats in family

words.note: Feminine. en famille is the set phrase — with the family, as a household — and it takes no article at all.
Capitalised, and it carries an -s that is part of the word rather than a plural. à Pâques, exactly like à Noël.

sentences.trap: en famille has no article and no possessive. avec ma famille exists and means something narrower — this phrase means at home, together, the way it is done.
sentences.sound: a no-EL on mahnzh ahn fa-MEEY.

variations.display: À Pâques on mange en famille
variations.cue: At Easter we eat with family
variations.changed: the other festival, the same custom

variations.display: À Noël on mange chez mes parents
variations.cue: At Christmas we eat at my parents'
variations.changed: L3-M2's chez, naming the house

mistake.display: À Noël on mange avec la famille
mistake.why: Understandable, but the phrase French uses is en famille. À Noël on mange en famille.

sentences.usage: Answering what do you do at Christmas? in the voice a French person would use.
sentences.mnemonic: en famille: no article, no possessive, no argument.

sentences.display: À Noël on offre des cadeaux aux enfants
sentences.cue: At Christmas we give presents to the children
sentences.literal: At Christmas one offers some presents to-the children

words.note: Irregular: j'offre, on offre, ils offrent. donner is to hand over; offrir is to give as a present, and it is the verb a festival uses.
Masculine, plural in -x like gâteau. offrir un cadeau à quelqu'un — the person takes à, and aux when it is les.

sentences.trap: donner un cadeau is understood and sounds like handing over a parcel. The verb for a present is offrir, and French keeps the two apart.
sentences.sound: a no-EL on OFR day ka-DOH oh zahn-FAHN.

variations.display: On offre un cadeau à ma sœur
variations.cue: We give a present to my sister
variations.changed: one present, and à before a named person

variations.display: Il faut offrir un cadeau
variations.cue: You have to bring a present
variations.changed: L3-M8's il faut in front of the infinitive

mistake.display: À Noël on donne des cadeaux
mistake.why: A present is offert, not donné. À Noël on offre des cadeaux.

sentences.usage: The single most useful sentence about a French December.
sentences.mnemonic: You offer a present in French; you only hand over a parcel.

sentences.display: La fête nationale est le quatorze juillet
sentences.cue: The national holiday is the fourteenth of July
sentences.literal: The festival national is the fourteen July

words.note: Feminine here because fête is feminine, and it follows its noun — French puts most adjectives after, where English puts them before.
The plain number, not an ordinal. Only the first of the month is different: le premier, with L2-M4's premier.
Lowercase, like every French month. Note the spelling — juillet, not *juilliet — and that juin is a different month.

sentences.trap: English says the fourteenth of July and needs two words French does not have: no -th, and no of. le quatorze juillet is the whole date.
sentences.sound: la fet na-syo-NAL eh luh ka-TORZ zhwee-YEH.

variations.display: La fête nationale est en juillet
variations.cue: The national holiday is in July
variations.changed: en for the month alone, with no date

variations.display: Le quatorze juillet, c'est la fête nationale
variations.cue: The fourteenth of July is the national holiday
variations.changed: the date first, which is how it is usually said

mistake.display: La fête nationale est le quatorzième de juillet
mistake.why: No ordinal and no de. La fête nationale est le quatorze juillet.

sentences.usage: The date every conversation in France turns to in the middle of the summer.
sentences.mnemonic: Plain number, no of — only the first of the month is an ordinal.

sentences.display: Mon anniversaire est le premier mai
sentences.cue: My birthday is the first of May
sentences.literal: My birthday is the first May

words.note: Masculine, and it does both English words. Bon anniversaire is what you say; joyeux anniversaire is what the card prints.
Lowercase, three letters, and the shortest month name. Le premier mai is a public holiday in France.
Lowercase. Two pronunciations are both heard, oot and a-OO, and the a can be silent — nobody will correct you either way.

sentences.trap: le premier is the one date that takes an ordinal. Every other day of the month is the plain number, so le deuxième mai is wrong and le deux mai is right.
sentences.sound: mon a-nee-vehr-SEHR eh luh pruh-myay MEH.

variations.display: Mon anniversaire est le quatorze août
variations.cue: My birthday is the fourteenth of August
variations.changed: a plain number, and a different month

variations.display: Son anniversaire est en janvier
variations.cue: Her birthday is in January
variations.changed: en with the month, when the day does not matter

mistake.display: Mon anniversaire est le un mai
mistake.why: The first of the month is an ordinal. Mon anniversaire est le premier mai.

sentences.usage: Answering the question every French form and every French colleague asks.
sentences.mnemonic: First is special; everything after it is just a number.

sentences.display: Le Nouvel An est le premier janvier
sentences.cue: New Year's Day is the first of January
sentences.literal: The New Year is the first January

words.note: Both words capitalised, and nouvel rather than nouveau because an begins with a vowel. The evening before is le réveillon.
Lowercase, like every month. en janvier for the month, le premier janvier for the day.
Lowercase, and the month Noël sits in: Noël est le vingt-cinq décembre.

sentences.trap: The month is lowercase and the festival is not: le premier janvier, but le Nouvel An. English capitalises both and gives no warning that French splits them.
sentences.sound: luh noo-vel AHN eh luh pruh-myay zhahn-VYAY.

variations.display: Noël est en décembre
variations.cue: Christmas is in December
variations.changed: en with a bare month, and no date at all

variations.display: Le Nouvel An, on mange en famille
variations.cue: At New Year we eat with family
variations.changed: the custom sentence, with on doing the work

mistake.display: Le nouvel an est le premier Janvier
mistake.why: The capitals are the wrong way round: le Nouvel An, le premier janvier.

sentences.usage: Wishing someone well in the first week of the year.
sentences.mnemonic: Festivals get capitals; months do not.

sentences.display: Le dimanche je ne travaille pas
sentences.literal: The Sunday I not work not

words.note: The article makes it a habit. Without it — dimanche je ne travaille pas — it is this coming Sunday and nothing more. L2-M6 taught the bare day.

sentences.trap: There is no preposition here in either reading. je ne travaille pas le dimanche, never *sur le dimanche — English's on has nothing to become.
sentences.sound: luh dee-MAHNSH zhuh nuh tra-vy PA.

variations.display: Dimanche je ne travaille pas
variations.cue: I'm not working on Sunday
variations.changed: the article gone, so it is one Sunday only

variations.display: Le dimanche on mange en famille
variations.cue: On Sundays we eat with family
variations.changed: the habit reading, with on

mistake.display: Sur le dimanche je ne travaille pas
mistake.why: A day takes no preposition. Le dimanche je ne travaille pas.

sentences.usage: Describing your week, which is where the two readings get confused.
sentences.mnemonic: Add the article and one Sunday becomes every Sunday.

sentences.display: En août, on est en vacances
sentences.literal: In August, one is in holidays

words.note: Always plural, and it takes en: être en vacances, partir en vacances. There is no singular une vacance in this sense.

sentences.trap: vacances has no singular and takes en, not sur or à. je suis en vacances is the only shape of it a learner needs and the only one French offers.
sentences.sound: ahn OOT, on eh tahn va-KAHNS.

variations.display: En juillet, on est en vacances
variations.cue: In July we're on holiday
variations.changed: the other summer month, unchanged otherwise

variations.display: À Pâques, on est en vacances
variations.cue: At Easter we're on holiday
variations.changed: à for a festival, en for a month

mistake.display: En août, on est en vacance
mistake.why: The word is plural and stays plural. On est en vacances.

sentences.usage: Explaining why nothing in France answers the phone for four weeks.
sentences.mnemonic: à a festival, en a month — and vacances is never singular.
